what_it_does: Homomorphic encryption (HE) is a special form of encryption that lets a server compute on your data without ever decrypting it — meaning the server can answer questions about your private data while learning nothing. The catch is that HE operations are enormously expensive: a simple computation can take thousands of times longer than on ordinary data, and the encrypted data (called ciphertexts) are huge, so moving them around consumes most of the time. CIPHERMATCH focuses on the specific task of searching text strings under HE encryption. It redesigns the algorithm to eliminate the most expensive HE operations (multiplication and rotation), replacing them with cheaper additions only. It also packs the encrypted data more compactly to reduce how much needs to be moved, and places extra computation units directly adjacent to the storage chips (in-flash processing, meaning computation happens where the data lives rather than hauling data to a remote processor).
